findingDetails.title: Retrieval fixture retains one pre-rename phrase variant
findingDetails.evidence: The staged diff sweeps this fixture (e.g. 037-001-sk-code-opencode-standards-audit -> 037-001-sk-code-skilled-standards-audit; sk-code-opencode 1.0.0.0 -> sk-code-skilled 1.0.0.0), but the entry keyed 'sk code opencode rename impact' still maps to the variant 'sk-code-opencode rename impact'. Repo-wide sweep shows this is the only remaining old-identity string outside the documented exclusions.
findingDetails.userImpact: Fixture hygiene only: if a retrieval assertion uses the old-name phrase it is load-bearing; otherwise the fixture keeps a stale variant that no longer matches the renamed trigger set.
findingDetails.scopeProof: rg -n 'sk-code-opencode|code-opencode' over the worktree yields 3734 hit lines across 254 files: 201 specs machine records, 45 this-packet docs, 4 benchmark JSON reports (all excluded), 3 historical records (R1-P2-002), and this fixture line.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked for a sibling 'sk-code-skilled rename impact' entry (none) and for the packet's own research metadata still registering the old phrase (specs/sk-code/012-sk-code-skilled-rename/001-rename-impact-research/graph-metadata.json:20 - yes).
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The phrase may be a deliberate historical-query alias so old-name searches still find the rename packet, mirroring that packet's registered trigger phrase.
findingDetails.recommendation: Confirm intent; if deliberate, add the new-name sibling or a marker so the gap is visibly intentional; otherwise update the entry.
